Bit idea: Drug commercial with Side effects, return with those on face, "Thanks Certicort"
Expanded Concept: Full pharma-ad parody: HeadCase as the beaming spokesperson for Certicort. Cheerful pitch, then the fast-voiced disclaimer kicks in and each spoken side effect hits his TV face live - droopy-eye filter, pixel scramble, color inversion, slow spin - while he keeps smiling through it. Wraps on glassy sincerity: "Thanks, Certicort."
Programmatic / Tech Steps: Pre-build 4-5 face-distortion filters, one app button each. Record the disclaimer VO with cue markers; rear screens run soft pharma b-roll (meadows, families, sunsets) that glitches in sync with each side effect. One macro fires the full sequence; keep manual buttons for live recovery.
Notes / Risks: VO-to-filter timing needs rehearsal. Cap at 4-5 distortions or it reads messy. Keep side effects absurd, not disturbing, to hold PG. Make sure the fake drug name doesn't collide with a real brand.
Outline Dialog/Steps: 1) HeadCase beams as pitchman: happy-face + meadow b-roll (SCREEN: head happy filter, rear pharma b-roll). 2) Pitch 3 product benefits, each lands a small laugh. 3) FAST VO disclaimer starts (SCREEN: macro begins). 4) Each side effect = one face distortion: droopy eye -> pixel scramble -> color invert -> slow spin, hold each ~2s (LAUGH BREAK each). 5) Deeper voice side effect on the spin. 6) Snap back to beaming face: 'Thanks, Certicort.' (SCREEN: b-roll returns) - button ending, hold 3s.
Assets Needed: 4-5 face-distortion filters; disclaimer VO with cue markers; pharma b-roll (meadows/family/sunset); glitch SFX; macro wiring all cues; fake-drug logo card.

Bit idea: Headcase out of costume needs to wear a giant hat with an iad in it, or a regular hat with an phone above the bill
Expanded Concept: The screen-head "turns off" when he's off duty - so he wears substitute faces: a giant brim hat with an iPad strapped in looping a static face, or a ball cap with a phone clipped above the bill playing a bored-face video. Crowd realization: the TV never actually turns off.
Programmatic / Tech Steps: iPad/phone mounted in or onto the hat, looping a pre-rendered face video (or a reactive face app). Lock brightness, disable auto-lock and notifications, hide a battery pack in the hat band. Optional Bluetooth trigger to tap-change faces.
Notes / Risks: Weight and heat - keep the rig under ~1.5 lb and ventilated. Mount above eye line so back rows can read it. Kill all notifications before showtime; nothing dies faster than a calendar ping on his forehead.
Outline Dialog/Steps: OFFSTAGE build. 1) Mount device in hat, loop face video. 2) Walk-through test: weight, sight lines, heat. 3) IN SHOW: worn on entry/exit only; crowd realizes the 'off-duty head' is still a screen (LAUGH: the realization, no button needed).
Assets Needed: Hat rig + mount; 1 looping face video (bored/deadpan); battery pack; notification lockdown checklist.

Assets Needed: Face video sliced into N tile clips; sync-start playlists per phone; master trigger button; optional crowd-cam pass-through config; phone mounts + battery bank.

Bit idea: Is this on, turn tv off, sight Gag
Expanded Concept: Classic tech-check opener. HeadCase taps his temple: "Is this thing on?" Offstage tech "fixes" it by switching the TV OFF - face goes black with a power icon, he stands deadpan in total silence... then the face pops back on color bars and he carries on like nothing happened.
Programmatic / Tech Steps: Two app buttons: POWER OFF (full-black face + soft power-down chime, rear screens dim with it) and POWER ON (color bars / broadcast test pattern, then back to normal face). Hold the black beat 3-5 seconds. Bonus third beat: an "auto-play next episode in 5..." countdown before the face returns.
Notes / Risks: The silence is the joke - hold it, don't rush. Brief backstage not to touch real cues during the blackout. Check house-light spill so the deadpan reads from the back.
Outline Dialog/Steps: 1) Walk out tapping temple: 'Is this thing on? Is the TV on?' (SCREEN: normal). 2) Offstage voice: 'Try turning it off and on again.' 3) BUTTON: face goes full black + power-down chime (SCREEN: black + tiny power icon; rear screens dim). 4) Total silence, deadpan - hold 3-5s (THE LAUGH BREAK). 5) BUTTON: color bars pop on (SCREEN: test pattern + tone). 6) Beat 2: 'Auto-play next episode in 5...' countdown. 7) Face returns mid-sentence, carry on like nothing happened.
Assets Needed: Power-off face card (black + power icon); power-down chime; color-bars card + tone; 'auto-play next episode' countdown graphic; macro + manual overrides.

Bit idea: Let watch something funny
Expanded Concept: HeadCase announces "let's watch something funny" and flips his own face through channels: static, a fishing show, a cat video, an eternal loading spinner... then gives up, turns the face-cam on the audience - "oh, this is good" - and just watches them. The crowd becomes the content.
Programmatic / Tech Steps: Button 1: channel-surf macro cycling static burst -> 2-3 licensed/stock clips -> loading spinner. Button 2: rear-facing camera pass-through so the audience sees themselves live on his screen. Keep camera latency under ~200ms so the mirror feels real.
Notes / Risks: Latency kills the mirror gag - test the full camera chain in the room. Crowd shots need camera gain for dim venues. Only use clips you actually have rights to (stock library or self-shot).
Outline Dialog/Steps: 1) 'Alright, let's watch something funny.' 2) Channel-surf macro: static burst -> fishing show (2s) -> cat video (2s) -> infomercial snippet (LAUGH BREAK) -> eternal loading spinner ('come on...'). 3) Give up: 'You know what? YOU'RE funny.' 4) BUTTON: face-cam mirrors audience (SCREEN: live crowd on his face, <200ms latency). 5) Just watch; react to real crowd moments (open LAUGH BREAK). 6) Out: 'This is a good one.'
Assets Needed: Channel-surf clip stack (static, 2-3 licensed stock clips, spinner) + surf SFX; rear-facing camera + low-latency pass-through config; gain settings for dim rooms.

Bit idea: Talk to max headroom

Programmatic / Tech Steps: Pre-render 6-8 short character clips (stutter edit + glitch overlays + retro studio backdrop). Cut them as clean answers so HeadCase can trade lines live with rehearsed timing; each clip + glitch stinger sits on its own button. Rear screen for full-frame, head PIP for reaction shots.

Outline Dialog/Steps: 1) Ringtone glitch: incoming 'call' (SCREEN: retro glitch UI). 2) Answer: Max Halftone stutters in on rear screen (SCREEN: full-frame character clip, retro studio backdrop). 3) Trade 4-5 rehearsed lines - who's the real TV head (LAUGH BREAK each trade). 4) He interrupts one of HeadCase's answers (glitch stinger). 5) HeadCase wins the feed: 'Bad signal, sorry.' Abort button if timing slips. 60-90s hard cap.
Assets Needed: 6-8 pre-rendered Halftone clips (stutter edit + glitch overlays + retro backdrop); glitch stinger SFX; bad-signal abort card; PIP layout for head reactions.
